alerts.reason: Net product sales growth slowed from about 15.1% in the first nine months to 3.8% in the December quarter, calculated from A and B. Higher realized prices drove most of the growth (D). A further slowdown as those prices enter the prior-year comparison supports a forecast above −5% in January–March and at or below −5% in April–June.

Bookings fell 4.4% to $8.0 billion while reported annual revenue fell only 0.8% to $8.4 billion (A, B). Existing orders could support January–March revenue, but bookings running roughly $400 million below sales and lower volumes in several businesses (D) point to a decline of at least 5% by April–June.

Net sales rose 5.0%, but deliveries outpaced new orders and backlog fell 37.6%, from $912.7 million to $569.8 million (A–C). The remaining orders could keep the March-quarter sales change above −5%. Continued deliveries from a much smaller backlog support a decline of at least 5% in April–June.

Cerence recognized $67.8 million of deferred revenue early in the December quarter, exceeding its entire $54.6 million year-over-year revenue gain by $13.2 million (A, C). That leaves less revenue to recognize in later quarters. I forecast the crossing in April–June, with timing uncertain because C does not give the original recognition schedule.

Reported annual operating revenue fell just 0.2%. Acquisition-driven shipments lifted Truckload Logistics revenue 32% even as revenue per shipment fell (A, B). One-Way Truckload revenue per mile excluding fuel surcharges also fell 5.5% (D). As the acquired shipments enter the prior-year comparison, those rate declines could take consolidated revenue growth from above −5% in January–March to at or below −5% in April–June.
